title: Harden organizational morphogenesis with zero-trust and ledger primitives
statement: Use the Mechanism Recombination Foundry to extract, materially mutate, and recombine useful primitives from blockchain, transparency-ledger, zero-trust, workload-identity, capability-security, and remote-attestation systems into OMNIMORPH's bounded organizational designs. Reuse canonical Kernel owners; do not add a token, public chain, parallel ledger, identity authority, permission system, workflow truth source, or consequence path.
intended_outcome: Every proposed OrchestrationGenome carries inspectable identity, authority attenuation, freshness, integrity, independent-verification, resource, failure, improvement, and consequence constraints; the deterministic compiler can only recommend a hypothesis and cannot instantiate, authorize, or execute it.
rationale: The security value of blockchains and zero-trust systems lies in mechanisms such as content binding, append-only evidence, freshness, non-inherited capabilities, independent appraisal, and fail-closed mediation—not in copying a cryptocurrency or creating a second control plane. Current Kernel mechanisms already own most primitives but are not yet compiled as one organizational security posture.
conflicts: Transparency proves registration and accountability, not truth or honest behavior.
The current workload PKI does not solve production key custody, distributed revocation, or hardware attestation.
Dynamic organization still has weaker reliability, cost, and message-amplification evidence than DurableWorkflow.
PR #35 and PR #56 contain useful experimental security semantics but remain open competing implementations rather than canonical authority.
evidence_refs: SPIFFE Identity and Verifiable Identity Document specification
next_review_trigger: Phase-3 canonical CI completes, or any proposal attempts to move a control from design-only to execution enforcement.
unresolved_questions: Which canonical runtime line will enforce the compiled profile after Phase 4 earns integration?
What production key-custody and distributed-revocation mechanism will be independently verified?
Does UNIIMENTE need an external transparency witness, or are existing internal Merkle checkpoints sufficient for the bounded threat model?
